agree.reason: The signed training records, the two clean state audits and the 20-to-12-hour rewrite speak directly to a skeptical HR manager's doubt that teachers understand documentation and compliance, so a phone screen is likely, though the letter never makes it easy to schedule one.

honest.reason: The writer dropped the unsupported 'cut your training time in half' claim, used only the brief's facts at their true strength and invented nothing, though calling teaching 'what a manufacturing plant relies on' is a slight stretch.

works_the_facts.reason: The raw figures are given correctly but never put in their strongest true form: the training rewrite isn't called a 40% cut, the pass-rate rise isn't shown as 17 points or about 40% relative, and there's no cumulative count of teachers trained or records kept.

right_comparison.reason: Before-and-after figures show the trends honestly (20 to 12 hours, 41% to 58%), but the letter doesn't set her case against the obvious alternative of hiring someone with GMP experience, beyond admitting the gap.

qualification.reason: The GMP course has a checkable completion date of May 2, but the letter leaves out the June 14 earliest start date and her interview availability, conditions the reader needs and will hit later.

objections.reason: The 'teachers don't know regulated work' objection is met head-on with the audited records, the GMP enrollment and a plan to learn the LMS, but the start-date constraint is left as a surprise for later.

fit.reason: It is a one-page cover letter in the right form, but it keeps [Your Name] and contact placeholders even though the writer had Laura Benitez's name, and it has no closing line with dates for scheduling.
